pages.title: A Green Plan for Europe
pages.content:
The European Union (EU) is a group of countries in Europe. The European Commission works for the EU. On 11 December 2019, it showed a new plan to the world. The name of the plan is the Green Deal.

Today, cars and factories send bad gases into the air. These gases make our world hot. The Green Deal wants a clean world. The EU wants net zero in 2050. Gas goes into the air. Then the same gas comes out of the air.

The plan also says, “Use less, and throw away less.” People can use old things again.

vocabulary.definition: What you want to do and how.
A building where people make things.
It is all around us; we need it.
Something like air; we cannot see it.
Same gas in and out of the air.

pages.title: Three Big Goals
pages.content:
The Green Deal has three big goals.

Goal 1 is about the climate. Our world is getting hotter. This is a big problem for all countries. The EU wants 55% less bad gas in 2030. It wants net zero in 2050.

Goal 2 is about nature. Water and trees are very important. We should not cut too many trees. We should not use too much water. Plants and animals need a safe home. All people need clean water, clean air and good food.

Goal 3 is about work and money. The EU wants new green companies. Then people can have jobs, and nature can stay safe.

vocabulary.definition: Something you want to do in the future.

pages.title: Why Do We Need It?
pages.content:
Why is the Green Deal important? Our world is in danger. There is a lot of pollution in the air and in the water. The weather is changing, too.

For many years, people used oil, gas and coal for energy. Cars, homes and factories use them every day. But they make bad gases, and they are bad for nature. And one day, there will be no more oil, gas and coal. We cannot use them like this for a long time.

Energy is a big problem today, too. There are wars in some places. Some things from other countries cannot come on time. Then energy is very expensive.

pages.title: Energy from the Wind and the Sun
pages.content:
Now many countries use energy from the wind and the sun. This energy never ends, and it is often cheaper. With it, countries do not need expensive oil and gas.

Factories need a lot of energy. They need clean energy at a good price. The EU wants this change to be fast. Countries need a big plan. They also need a lot of money for new clean machines.

vocabulary.definition: Air that moves fast outside.
How much money something is.

pages.title: New Machines for Clean Energy
pages.content:
In 20 or 30 years, the world can be net zero. Then there will be new jobs, new machines and new kinds of energy. Some countries start early and work fast. They can be the best in the world at clean energy.

The EU has a law for this. Its name is the Net-Zero Industry Act. With this law, factories in Europe can make batteries, solar panels and big wind machines. They can also make machines that take bad gas out of the air.

vocabulary.definition: A thing that does work for us.

It makes energy from the sun.

pages.title: Repair and Reuse
pages.content:
The EU has new rules for green things, too. Here are two examples.

Rule 1: Big companies in the EU mustn’t throw away new clothes. Sometimes people do not buy some clothes, but the companies mustn’t throw them away. That is waste.

Rule 2: It is easy to find parts for machines. Then people can repair their old things and use them again.

Soon, there will be rules like these for a lot of things.

pages.title: Smart Shopping and Green Jobs
pages.content:
Shoppers are important, too. Before they buy something, they need good information. Look at a new TV. It has an energy label. The label tells you about the TV’s energy. Then you can choose the green one.

Jobs are changing, too. There are more green jobs every year. People need new skills for these jobs. Countries need training for these people.

pages.title: Learning and Working Together
pages.content:
Education is a big part of the Green Deal. All people can learn green skills and computer skills. Then we can all help our world.

Countries, companies and people can all help. Climate change is a problem for every country. Countries should work together.

Türkiye has a Green Deal plan, too. Türkiye made it in 2021. Türkiye wants net zero in 2053.

vocabulary.definition: Teaching and learning, at school and at work.

terms.definition: The usual weather in a place.

terms.definitionAr: هَوَاءٌ أَوْ مَاءٌ أَوْ أَرْضٌ غَيْرُ نَظِيفَةٍ.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review the language from all chapters.

exercises.title: Look: One or Many
exercises.question: Which form is right?

formChoices.sentence: The label [choice] you about the TV’s energy.

exercises.explanation: One thing (the EU, the label) + verb + -s. Many things (factories) + verb.

feedback.incorrect: One thing: add -s. Many things: no -s.

exercises.title: Practise: Should or Mustn’t?
exercises.instructions: Put each sentence in the right group.
exercises.question: Should or mustn’t?

items: We should not use too much water.
Big companies mustn’t throw away new clothes.

Good to do (should): We should not use too much water.
Do not do it (mustn’t): Big companies mustn’t throw away new clothes.

exercises.explanation: Should = it is good to do it. Mustn’t = a rule: do not do it.

feedback.incorrect: Chapter 2 and 8: should. Chapter 6: mustn’t.

exercises.title: Practise: Is, Are, Will Be
exercises.question: Which words go in the gap?

formChoices.sentence: There [choice] new jobs in the future.

exercises.explanation: There is + one. There are + many. There will be = in the future.

feedback.incorrect: Find these sentences in Chapters 3 and 5.

exercises.title: Practise: Hotter, Cheaper, The Best
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: Which word goes in the gap?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Our world is getting [blank]. Energy from the wind and the sun is often [blank]. Some countries can be the [blank] in the world at clean energy.
exercises.explanation: Hot → hotter. Cheap → cheaper. Good → the best.

feedback.incorrect: Find these words in Chapters 2, 4 and 5.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Choose the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?

errorItems.sentence: The European Commission work for the EU.

exercises.explanation: The European Commission = one: works. Should never takes -s.

feedback.incorrect: One thing + verb + -s. Should + verb, no -s.

exercises.title: Use: My Green Plan
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences: your green plan.
exercises.question: What is your green plan?
exercises.explanation: Use should, mustn’t and can + verb.

discussionPrompts.question: One “mustn’t”: “We mustn’t …”
discussionPrompts.example: We mustn’t throw away good food.

discussionPrompts.question: One “can”: “I can …”
discussionPrompts.example: I can repair my old bike.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole book together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: The EU
exercises.question: What is the EU?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The European Union (EU) is a group of [blank] in Europe.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “The European Union (EU) is a group of countries in Europe.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentence of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Goal 3
exercises.question: What does the EU want for Goal 3?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “The EU wants new green companies.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the Goal 3 paragraph of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Oil, Gas and Coal
exercises.question: One day, there will be no more oil, gas and coal.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “And one day, there will be no more oil, gas and coal.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: What Is It?
exercises.instructions: Match the word with the sentence.
exercises.question: What is it?

matchingPairs.right: It makes energy from the sun.
It tells you about a machine’s energy.
It gives energy to phones and cars.

correctAnswer.a solar panel: It makes energy from the sun.
correctAnswer.an energy label: It tells you about a machine’s energy.
correctAnswer.a battery: It gives energy to phones and cars.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: batteries and solar panels. Chapter 7: the energy label.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 5 and 7 again.

exercises.title: The Law
exercises.question: What is the name of the EU law?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “Its name is the Net-Zero Industry Act.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Clothes
exercises.question: Big companies in the EU can throw away new clothes.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “Big companies in the EU mustn’t throw away new clothes.”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is false. They mustn’t.
feedback.incorrect: Read the Rule 1 paragraph of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: Green Jobs
exercises.question: What do people need for green jobs?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “People need new skills for these jobs.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: The Years
exercises.question: What comes first?

sequencingItems.text: 2019: The European Commission shows the Green Deal.
2021: Türkiye makes its Green Deal plan.
2030: The EU wants 55% less bad gas.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: 2019 and 2050. Chapter 2: 2030. Chapter 8: 2021.

feedback.correct: Great! You know the years of the Green Deal.
feedback.incorrect: Find the years in Chapters 1, 2 and 8.
